summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever one month after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He had recently been treated for a surgical site infection and was on antibiotics, raising concern for C. difficile colitis. Initial evaluation included an abdominal ultrasound that ruled out a fluid collection or abscess in the gallbladder fossa. Stool testing confirmed C. difficile infection, and he was started on intravenous metronidazole, later transitioned to oral therapy. His symptoms improved steadily, with decreasing bowel movements and resolution of fever. He remained stable throughout the admission with no signs of liver decompensation. His home medications were continued, and he was discharged home with a full course of oral metronidazole, instructions to avoid alcohol, and follow-up arranged with his liver specialist.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, unspecified
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
